blocked_claims.statement: Hybrid statistically outperforms Machine Learning or Rule-based diagnosis.
The reported metrics generalize to real-world or unseen production networks.
The 96 deterministic masks are independent experimental samples.
The system diagnoses simultaneous multiple faults.
The system supports OSPF or arbitrary dynamic-routing failures.
The Dashboard performs live inference, remediation, or production network monitoring.
The accepted confidence values are statistically calibrated uncertainty estimates.
The accepted results establish population-level statistical significance.

claim_matrix.limit: The claim is limited to the implemented local Containerlab contexts and approved single-fault taxonomy.
claim_matrix.statement: The project implements a controlled-laboratory pipeline from fault injection and passive evidence collection through diagnosis, evaluation, restoration, and dataset construction.

claim_matrix.limit: Rows are controlled laboratory observations, not a representative sample of production networks.
claim_matrix.statement: The final clean dataset covers six diagnostic classes in six complete contexts with a whole-context 36/12/24 train/validation/test split.

claim_matrix.limit: The comparison is descriptive and contains no statistical-superiority test.
claim_matrix.statement: Rule-based, Machine Learning, and Hybrid methods are compared under the same frozen report-only test protocol.

claim_matrix.limit: Perfect clean-set results do not establish performance outside E02/E06 or beyond the controlled taxonomy.
claim_matrix.statement: All three accepted methods achieve complete fault-type classification on the 24 clean final test inputs.

claim_matrix.limit: The 96 masked inputs are transformations of 24 clean inputs, not independent network experiments.
claim_matrix.statement: Under four deterministic missing-evidence masks, the strict Rule-based method fails closed while the accepted Machine Learning and Hybrid methods retain full coverage and non-zero aggregate accuracy.

claim_matrix.limit: Its final aggregate metrics equal the Machine Learning method; no Hybrid performance advantage is claimed.
claim_matrix.statement: The Hybrid method implements a rule-first, Machine-Learning-fallback decision policy with auditable provenance.

claim_matrix.limit: The interface is not a live diagnosis service, production NMS, or remote deployment.
claim_matrix.statement: Accepted evidence, predictions, comparisons, and limitations can be inspected through a local fail-closed read-only interface.

claim_matrix.limit: This establishes protocol integrity for the accepted run, not independent external replication.
claim_matrix.statement: The final evaluation preserves train/validation/test roles, verifies the development freeze before test access, and records one report-only test attempt without refit or test-guided revision.

findings.limit: This is confined to the controlled final test contexts and taxonomy.
findings.statement: All three methods have 1.0 clean accuracy and 1.0 clean macro-F1 on 24 accepted clean inputs.

findings.limit: The 96 inputs are transformations of 24 clean inputs, not independent experiments.
findings.statement: On 96 deterministic masked inputs, Rule-based accuracy, macro-F1, and coverage are 0.0 while insufficient-evidence rate is 1.0.

findings.limit: This descriptive equality does not establish statistical superiority or real-world generalization.
findings.statement: On masked inputs, Machine Learning and Hybrid both have accuracy 0.7916666666666666, macro-F1 0.8104858104858105, and coverage 1.0.

findings.limit: No Hybrid performance-advantage claim is authorized.
findings.statement: Hybrid is operationally distinct through rule-first and Machine-Learning-fallback provenance, but its accepted aggregate metrics equal Machine Learning in every scope.

findings.limit: No statistical-superiority test or independent external replication was performed.
findings.statement: The comparison is descriptive, follows one frozen report-only test attempt, and records no refit, policy reselection, or test-guided revision.
